newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels want countries to stop mercenaries.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels want countries to stop mercenaries.

text.p: Rebels fighting to overthrow Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko called on France, Belgium, South Africa and others on Wednesday to stop their citizens joining a mercenary force supporting the army.

"We want to dissuade these countries from allowing their people to serve a criminal and prolong his stay in power," the rebels' foreign affairs spokesman Kakudji Gaetan told a news conference in Goma.
Kakudji said mercenaries from France, Belgium, South Africa, Angola and Togo were being assembled by Mobutu along with soldiers of the Hutu former Rwandan army in exile in Zaire..

In little over three months the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) has overrun a slice of eastern Zaire 600 km (400 miles) long bordering Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Tuesday said the army was preparing to launch a counterattack.

Kakudji said the mercenaries were based at Kisangani 600 km (400 miles) from the border, at Kindu 400 km (250 miles) away and at Wadja 600 km (400 miles) to the north, the site of a strategic airstrip.
The rebels say the Angolans are fighters of Jonas Savimbi's UNITA movement which fought a 20-year civil war against the Angolan government using rear bases in Zaire with the blessing of Mobutu.
They also accuse South Africa's private security firm Executive Outcomes of helping the Zaire army.

"Executive Outcomes were in Angola and Sierra Leone. Now they are here with Mobutu and we will drive them out along with the other murderers and the Rwandans who were reponsible for genocide," said rebel spokesman Bizima Karaha.
On Tuesday, Executive Outcomes denied it had sent mercenaries to join a "White Legion" reported assembling in Zaire to help Kinshasa's army stem advances by the Rwandan-backed rebels.
Managing director of the Pretoria-based firm, Eeben Barlow, told Reuters: "We've never been in Zaire and we're never been asked by the Zairean authorities to go there."
The Paris daily Le Monde reported that a force of South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican mercenaries had gathered in eastern Zaire.
Le Monde said the force numbered between 200 and 300 but was expected to grow rapidly when more men left Europe in two weeks to join the soldiers of fortune on the spot.
During his 31-year rule Mobutu has on several occasions employed mercenaries and foreign troops to put down rebellions against his authority in the vast central African nation.
